## Problem Statement

New users face a blank platform: the first workbench, first pipeline, and first
model deployment all start from empty forms, and time-to-first-success is
measured in days. We want a curated tutorial gallery in the Dashboard — a set
of maintained, tested tutorials (notebooks and pipelines) that users can launch
into their own project with one click. This requires product code (the gallery
and launch mechanics), authored content (the tutorials themselves), and
documentation — three different kinds of work with different owners and review
processes.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | The Dashboard has a tutorial gallery from which a user can launch a tutorial into their project (opening a workbench with the notebook, or importing the pipeline). |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Six curated tutorials exist covering the core journeys: first workbench, data prep, first training run, first pipeline, first deployment, first RAG app. Each is tested against the current release. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | A tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images, validation manifest) is defined so tutorials are versioned and testable independently of Dashboard releases. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation covers using the gallery and the contribution process for new tutorials. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Notebooks
- Data Science Pipelines
- Documentation

## Out of Scope

- Partner- or community-contributed tutorial intake (contribution process is
  documented, but no submission tooling this release)
- Localization of tutorial content

## Open Questions

None.

# Define the tutorial packaging format and validation mechanism

## Description

This epic defines the tutorial packaging format — the contract that makes
curated tutorials versioned, testable, and launchable independently of
Dashboard releases. It produces the format specification (tutorial metadata,
pinned images, validation manifest) together with the validation mechanism
that checks a packaged tutorial against the format. The Dashboard tutorial
gallery and all authored tutorial content build against this contract.

## Scope

- Specify the tutorial packaging format covering:
  - Tutorial metadata (identity, journey category, display information)
  - Pinned images (workbench images and other referenced images pinned by
    digest or tag so tutorials run reproducibly)
  - A validation manifest describing how the tutorial is tested
- Define format versioning so a tutorial's packaging version is tracked
  independently of Dashboard releases
- Provide a validation mechanism (tooling or procedure) that validates a
  packaged tutorial against the format and reports pass/fail
- Keep the format applicable to both notebook-based tutorials and pipeline
  import tutorials

## Acceptance Criteria

- The packaging format specification documents the metadata fields, the image
  pinning rules, and the validation manifest structure.
- A tutorial packaged per the format carries a format version, and the
  versioning scheme allows tutorials to be updated without a Dashboard
  release.
- The validation mechanism, run against a packaged tutorial, produces a
  deterministic pass/fail result covering the checks declared in the
  tutorial's validation manifest.
- The format is demonstrated to describe at least one notebook-style tutorial
  and at least one pipeline-import-style tutorial.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): A tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images, validation
  manifest) is defined so tutorials are versioned and testable independently
  of Dashboard releases. Full coverage. (Epic priority is P0 by inheritance:
  the gallery and all tutorial content build against this format.)

# Dashboard tutorial gallery with one-click launch

## Description

This epic delivers the tutorial gallery in the Dashboard: a browsable,
curated gallery of getting-started tutorials from which a user can launch a
tutorial into their own project with one click — opening a workbench with the
notebook for notebook tutorials, or importing the pipeline for pipeline
tutorials.

## Scope

- Add the tutorial gallery surface to the Dashboard (listing curated
  tutorials with their metadata from the tutorial packaging format)
- Implement one-click launch into the user's own data science project:
  - For notebook tutorials: provision a workbench in the target project with
    the tutorial's notebook and pinned image
  - For pipeline tutorials: import the tutorial's pipeline into the project's
    Data Science Pipelines instance
- Read tutorial metadata, pinned images, and packaging version from the
  tutorial packaging format so gallery content updates without a Dashboard
  release
- Follow existing Dashboard integration patterns (navigation, project-scoped
  access, per-component feature flags via OdhDashboardConfig)

## Acceptance Criteria

- A user can open the tutorial gallery from the Dashboard and browse the
  curated tutorials with their metadata.
- Given a user with a data science project, selecting a notebook tutorial and
  choosing launch provisions a workbench in that project containing the
  tutorial's notebook, using the pinned image from its packaging.
- Given a user with a project that has a Data Science Pipelines instance,
  selecting a pipeline tutorial and choosing launch imports the tutorial's
  pipeline into that project.
- Launching a tutorial requires no manual copy/paste or file upload by the
  user (one click from gallery to running tutorial).
- End-to-end launch is verified against at least one real tutorial packaged
  per the tutorial packaging format against the current release.
- The tutorial gallery is gated by a per-component feature flag in
  OdhDashboardConfig: when the flag is disabled for the component, the gallery
  and its launch entry points are not shown to users; when enabled, the gallery
  is available.
- The gallery renders tutorial content driven by the packaging format, so
  adding or updating a tutorial does not require a Dashboard code change.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): The Dashboard has a tutorial gallery from which a user can
  launch a tutorial into their project (opening a workbench with the
  notebook, or importing the pipeline). Full coverage.

# Author and validate the curated notebook tutorials

## Description

This epic authors the notebook-based portion of the curated getting-started
tutorial set: five tested tutorials covering the core first-journeys — first
workbench, data prep, first training run, first deployment, and first RAG
app. Each tutorial is packaged per the tutorial packaging format and tested
against the current release.

## Scope

- Author five notebook tutorials covering the core journeys:
  1. First workbench — creating a project and starting a first workbench
  2. Data prep — loading and preparing data in a workbench
  3. First training run — training a first model
  4. First deployment — deploying the trained model for serving
  5. First RAG app — building a first retrieval-augmented generation app
- Package each tutorial per the tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned
  workbench images, validation manifest)
- Run each tutorial's validation against the current release so the set is
  verified working, not just written
- Keep content maintainable: concise, current-release-accurate notebooks that
  fail validation loudly when the platform moves underneath them

## Acceptance Criteria

- Five notebook tutorials exist covering the first workbench, data prep,
  first training run, first deployment, and first RAG app journeys.
- Each tutorial is packaged per the tutorial packaging format and passes the
  format's validation mechanism.
- Each tutorial has been executed successfully against the current release
  (validated, not merely authored).
- Each tutorial is launchable into a user's project as a workbench via the
  gallery's launch mechanics, using its pinned image.
- The five tutorials present a coherent progression from empty platform to a
  deployed model and a first RAG app.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0, partial — notebook journeys): Six curated tutorials exist
  covering the core journeys; each is tested against the current release.
  This epic covers five of the six journeys (first workbench, data prep,
  first training run, first deployment, first RAG app). The first-pipeline
  journey is covered by the pipeline tutorial epic.

# Document the tutorial gallery and contribution process

## Description

This epic delivers the user-facing documentation for the tutorial gallery:
how to browse and launch tutorials from the Dashboard, and how to contribute
new tutorials. Per the strategy's out-of-scope note, the contribution process
is documented but no submission tooling is built this release.

## Scope

Content outline:

- **Using the tutorial gallery**: what the gallery is, how to open it in the
  Dashboard, how to launch a tutorial into your own project (notebook
  tutorials opening a workbench; pipeline tutorials importing a pipeline),
  and what to expect while a tutorial runs
- **Contributing new tutorials**: the contribution process — the tutorial
  packaging format (metadata, pinned images, validation manifest), how
  tutorials are versioned and validated, and the review path for new tutorial
  content
- Cross-linking from existing getting-started documentation so new users
  reach the gallery early

## Acceptance Criteria

- A published documentation topic covers using the tutorial gallery,
  including launching notebook and pipeline tutorials into a project.
- A published documentation topic covers the tutorial contribution process,
  including the packaging format requirements and validation expectations.
- The documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented gallery
  and tutorial content (reviewed by or with the implementing teams), so it
  describes what actually ships.
- The documentation contains no submission-tooling instructions (intake
  tooling is out of scope this release; only the process is documented).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): Documentation covers using the gallery and the contribution
  process for new tutorials. Full coverage. (Epic priority is P1 per the
  docs-authoring priority exception derived from the strategy's Major
  priority, not from the HLR's P2 label.)

# Decomposition Summary — RHAISTRAT-9019 (Curated getting-started tutorial gallery)

## Triage

Not below threshold and not docs-only. The strategy explicitly spans three
distinct work streams — product code (gallery and launch mechanics in the
Dashboard), authored content (the tutorials themselves, spanning the Notebooks
and Data Science Pipelines components), and documentation — with different
owners and review processes. Multiple components and multiple teams are
affected, so full decomposition applies (Step 0 escape condition: multiple
distinct work streams).

## Strategy Parsing Notes

Parsed from the strategy file:

- **Affected Components**: Dashboard, Notebooks, Data Science Pipelines,
  Documentation (bullet list, no owner teams stated — teams below are taken
  from the architecture-context owning-team fields).
- **High Level Requirements**: HLR-1 (P0), HLR-2 (P0), HLR-3 (P1), HLR-4 (P2).
